content:
Yesterday we saw the earth and the fire, and we ended with a question.
The third judgment did not fall on the rebels or on the two hundred and fifty, but on the ordinary congregation who had just watched the first two judgments with their own eyes. What had they done, only a day later, to bring a plague into the camp? The plague teaches us that a hardened heart can spread.This third judgment is perhaps the most frightening of all, because it happened after the people had already seen the first two judgments. Numbers 16:41 says, "On the next day all the congregation... murmured against Moses and against Aaron." They had seen the earth open. They had seen the fire. Yet the very next day they were complaining again.

This is how a hardened heart works. A person listens to complaint, then joins the complaint, then stands with the rebellion, and eventually becomes so hardened that even correction produces blame rather than repentance. Then the plague came, and fourteen thousand seven hundred died (Numbers 16:49).
This gives the New Creation a frightening picture of sin spreading through a body. Paul uses similar language, "A little leaven leavens the whole lump"(1 Corinthians 5:6). One person's bitterness can infect a family. One person's gossip can poison a fellowship. One person's unbelief can discourage several believers. And one person's rebellion can become a group rebellion. Imagine that someone becomes offended with a brother in the church. Instead of speaking directly to him and seeking peace, he tells another person, "Do you know what this brother did to me?" Then that person tells another. Soon five people know only one side of the story. They begin interpreting everything that brother does in a negative way, until the original disagreement is no longer the real problem, because the spirit of complaint has spread. Complaining spreads unbelief, but prayer spreads faith, and Yahweh hears both. That is why Scripture commands, "Do all things without complaining and disputing" (Philippians 2:14). The plague gives us a picture of something that spreads if it is not stopped. Bitterness spreads, gossip spreads, jealousy spreads, false teaching spreads, immorality spreads, and unbelief spreads. A hardened heart can influence another hardened heart, until an entire fellowship is affected.

But now notice where the plague stopped, for here there is something beautiful. When the plague was spreading, Moses told Aaron to take his censer and make atonement for the congregation. Aaron ran into the middle of the people.

Then Scripture says, "He stood between the dead and the living; so the plague was stopped" (Numbers 16:48). Here, in the middle of judgment, we are suddenly brought to intercession. The people had rejected Aaron, yet Aaron stood between them and death. For the New Creation, this turns our eyes toward Christ Jesus, our great High Priest, of whom the Scripture says,"He always lives to make intercession for them" (Hebrews 7:25). When we fall, our answer is not to run farther into rebellion. We run toward our High Priest. John says, "If anyone sins, we have an Advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous" (1 John 2:1). This does not make deliberate sin safe. It makes repentance possible. Yahweh's holiness is real, but His correction calls His people back, rather than giving them permission to remain in sin.

So, the three judgments give the New Creation three searching questions.

The earth asks: what earthly thing is swallowing my spiritual life? The fire asks: am I treating Christ, His blood, His Word, or holy service casually? And the plague asks: is something sinful spreading through my heart, and from me into others? And Aaron standing between the living and the dead gives us the answer to all three: run to Christ our High Priest before rebellion hardens the heart. The earth, the fire, and the plague all show us the seriousness of sin,but the priest in the middle of the dying shows us the mercy that is still reaching out even while judgment falls.

Let us close with this reflection. The most dangerous condition is not that we stumble. It is that Yahweh corrects us, and we refuse to change. Israel saw the earth open and the fire fall, yet by the next morning they were murmuring again. Scripture therefore says, "Today, if you will hear His voice, do not harden your hearts" (Hebrews 3:15). When Yahweh exposes pride, we must repent. When He exposes jealousy, we must repent. When He exposes bitterness, we must repent. When He shows us that our tongue is poisoning others,we must stop speaking and make peace. And when earthly things begin swallowing our devotion, we must turn our eyes again toward Christ. For the safest heart is not the heart that never needs correction, but the heart that quickly bends when Yahweh corrects it.

title: Prayer
text:
O Yahweh, our God, whose holiness is perfect and whose mercy still reaches into the middle of judgment,
Guard us from the spirit of complaint that spreads like leaven through Your people.

Where we have carried an offence to others, teach us instead to go and make peace.

We thank You for Christ our High Priest, he ever lives to intercede for us.

When we fall, let us not run farther into rebellion, but run to our Advocate.

Make us the kind of heart that bends quickly the moment You correct us.

If anyone sins, we have an Advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous. - 1 John 2:1

In Christ name, our great High Priest, we pray. Amen.
